root.label: Value categories
root.note: Every C++ expression is classified by object identity and eligibility to be moved from.

children.label: Expression vs variable
children.note: Types belong to declarations whereas value categories describe evaluated expressions.

children.label: Named T&& parameter
children.note: A named rvalue-reference parameter has type T&& yet evaluates as an lvalue expression.

children.label: Function return types
children.note: Calls returning T, T&, and T&& produce prvalues, lvalues, and xvalues respectively.

children.label: Two orthogonal axes
children.note: Combining glvalue identity and rvalue movability partitions all expressions into three leaves.

children.label: lvalue (glvalue only)
children.note: Designates an existing addressable object or function that cannot be implicitly moved.

children.label: xvalue (glvalue and rvalue)
children.note: Designates an existing expiring object whose resources may be safely transferred.

children.label: prvalue (rvalue only)
children.note: Represents an unmaterialized computation or initializer with no storage address yet.

children.label: Temporary materialization
children.note: C++17 converts a prvalue to an xvalue only when an operation requires object identity.

children.label: Reference binding
children.note: Binding const T& or T&& materializes a prvalue into a temporary xvalue.

children.label: Member and array access
children.note: Reading a member or subscripting a temporary array triggers materialization first.

children.label: Discarded prvalue expression
children.note: Evaluating a standalone class prvalue materializes it so constructor and destructor run.

children.label: Subtle expression rules
children.note: Several common C++ expressions break naive left-of-equals intuition.

children.label: String vs numeric literals
children.note: String literals are static lvalues of const char[N], whereas numeric literals are prvalues.

children.label: Prefix vs postfix ++
children.note: Built-in ++i returns an lvalue to i while i++ yields a prvalue copy.

children.label: Member access E1.E2
children.note: A data member on an rvalue yields an xvalue, whereas a reference member yields an lvalue.

children.label: decltype probes
children.note: Parenthesized decltype((e)) reveals lvalue, xvalue, or prvalue directly in the type system.

children.label: Unparenthesized id-expression
children.note: decltype(x) inspects the declared type of x rather than its expression category.

children.label: Parenthesized expression
children.note: decltype((e)) produces T& for lvalues, T&& for xvalues, and T for prvalues.
